MAIN ANSWER: Pearson r = 0.0317 (full precision 0.03169390889798421) between gene Length and mean expression across the 132 CD14 samples, for n = 19,942 protein-coding genes (exact gene_biotype == "protein_coding"). Two-sided p = 7.59e-06; Fisher-z 95% CI = [0.0178, 0.0456]. The correlation is statistically significant (not noise) but very weak on the raw, untransformed scale.

Verified quantities you asked for:
- n genes = 19,942 (all protein-coding genes joined losslessly; 0 dropped), n samples = 132 (CD14 columns by regex CD14(_\d+)?$ == set of celltype=='CD14' samples, exact match; both L631 replicates kept).
- Protocol honored exactly: Length as supplied (bp, no rescaling); arithmetic mean of batch-corrected counts as-is; no low-count filtering, no CPM, no logs in the main computation; biotype not reclassified.

(1)(2) Main r: 0.0316939 (r²≈0.001 — gene length explains ~0.1% of variance of raw mean expression).
(3) Transformation sanity notes (NOT the answer): r(Length, log1p(mean_expr)) = 0.280389; r(log1p(Length), log1p(mean_expr)) = 0.375144. So the association is heavily masked by the heavy-tailed raw scale.
(4) p = 7.59e-06, 95% CI [0.0178, 0.0456] — a stable small positive value, not a tail artifact flipping sign; CI excludes 0 entirely.
(5) Skew diagnostics: median mean_expr = 39.74; max mean_expr = 354,289 (MT-CO1); genes with mean == 0: 1,849 (9.27%); Length median 4,336 bp, max 118,976 bp.

Honest leverage note you asked for: the raw r is NOT inflated by a handful of highly-expressed long genes — the opposite. The top-10 expressed genes are mostly SHORT (mitochondrial MT-CO1/MT-ND*, LYZ, ACTB), so on the raw scale these massive-value short genes pull the correlation toward zero/negative. Trimming the top 0.5% on both variables raises r from 0.032 → 0.166 (n=19,743, p=6.6e-122), and Spearman ρ = 0.399. Conclusion: there IS a real, robust positive length–expression association, but the mandated untransformed Pearson r on the raw count scale is only ≈ 0.032; report 0.0317 as the answer, with the log/Spearman figures as evidence that tail dominance suppresses it.

Sensitivity to biotype rule: contains('protein_coding') → n = 19,954, r = 0.031665 (Δ ≈ 3e-5) — confirms your call that exact-match vs contains is immaterial.

Deviations / exclusions (nothing fixed silently): (a) 12 compound-biotype genes excluded from main per your ruling (kept only in the sensitivity note); (b) 1,849 zero-mean genes retained (no filtering); (c) both L631 CD14 replicates retained; (d) no NA/dtype/duplicate issues found, so nothing was repaired.

Deliverable: concise answer r ≈ 0.0317; reproducible script attached as artifacts.analysis.
